accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the primary focus of the Neeru-Meeru programme?
o: Urban solid-waste management and sewage treatment
Construction of only major irrigation dams
Rainwater harvesting and raising groundwater levels
Large-scale inter-basin transfer of river water
accepted.x: Neeru-Meeru was a watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive intended to raise groundwater levels.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme by matching its stated objective.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: The Water Protection Board associated with the Neeru-Meeru programme was set up in:
accepted.x: The Water Protection Board was set up in 2002.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the programme launch year from the year of institutional formation.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Neeru-Chettu was launched in Andhra Pradesh on:
accepted.x: Neeru-Chettu was launched on 2 October 2014.
accepted.tq: Test the exact date attached to a government programme.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Neeru-Chettu:
1. It is a water-conservation sub-mission implemented across line departments.
2. The Water Resources Department is its nodal department.
3. Its works include tank desilting, bund strengthening and check dams on minor streams.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Neeru-Chettu operates across line departments under the Water Resources Department and includes the listed water-conservation works.
accepted.tq: Check whether the programme, nodal department and works are all correctly associated.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Under Neeru-Chettu, which one of the following is NOT specifically identified as a work?
o: Construction of nuclear power plants near reservoirs
Repair of sluices, weirs and shutters
accepted.x: Neeru-Chettu includes repairs, supply-channel desilting and tank-cascade development, but not construction of nuclear power plants.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s stated work profile.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: How many works were taken up under Neeru-Chettu, and what was their estimated value?
accepted.x: Neeru-Chettu covered 1,00,171 works at an estimated cost of ₹6,790 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its paired count and financial figure.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: The amount budgeted in 2025–26 for clearing pending Neeru-Chettu bills was:
accepted.x: ₹445.89 crore was budgeted in 2025–26 to clear pending Neeru-Chettu bills.
accepted.tq: Use precise budget-figure discrimination.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Jaladhara-Jalaharathi is associated with which of the following?
o: A 100-day water-conservation plan launched in April 2026
A five-year crop-insurance programme launched in 2024
accepted.x: Jaladhara-Jalaharathi is a 100-day water-conservation plan launched in April 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate similarly themed water programmes by their nature and launch period.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Jaladhara, the 100-day water-conservation action plan implemented with Water Users Associations, was launched at:
accepted.x: Jaladhara was launched at Yadiki in Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Test the exact place associated with a field-level programme launch.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes having an ayacut up to:
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes with an ayacut up to 5,000 acres.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Andhra Pradesh threshold from the national classification.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the national classification based on CCA?
o: Minor: up to 1,000 ha; Medium: 1,000–5,000 ha; Major: above 5,000 ha
Minor: up to 5,000 ha; Medium: 5,000–15,000 ha; Major: above 15,000 ha
Minor: up to 10,000 ha; Medium: 10,000–20,000 ha; Major: above 20,000 ha
Minor: up to 2,000 ha; Medium: 2,000–10,000 ha; Major: above 10,000 ha
accepted.x: Nationally, minor irrigation means CCA up to 2,000 ha, medium 2,000–10,000 ha and major above 10,000 ha.
accepted.tq: Compare classification thresholds carefully rather than applying the state-specific ayacut limit.
accepted.sec: Water harvesting and tank programmes - launch years

accepted.s: Which of the following river links is correctly matched with its stated feature?
o: Nagavali–Suvarnamukhi — intended for Rayalaseema irrigation only
Godavari–Penna Phase-I — a four-river link with no lifting component
accepted.x: The Godavari–Krishna link is functioning through Pattiseema. Vamsadhara–Nagavali was about 73% complete, Nagavali–Suvarnamukhi serves Vizianagaram drinking water, and Godavari–Penna Phase-I involves a five-stage lift.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure project-feature pair and eliminate reversed descriptions.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: The Polavaram Right Main Canal associated with the Godavari–Krishna link has a stated capacity of:
accepted.x: The Polavaram Right Main Canal is associated with an 80 TMC capacity in the Godavari–Krishna link.
accepted.tq: Test the project-specific capacity figure.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: Which combination correctly describes Godavari–Penna Phase-I?
accepted.x: Godavari–Penna Phase-I involves 73 TMC, a five-stage lift and 7,000 cusecs; it was approximately 21% complete.
accepted.tq: Match multiple quantitative attributes of a single project.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: The Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link, earlier known as the Banakacherla link, is intended to:
o: Link the Vamsadhara and Nagavali rivers exclusively for hydropower
Transfer Krishna water to coastal Odisha through Hirakud
Supply only drinking water to Vizianagaram through Suvarnamukhi
Transfer Godavari floodwater to Rayalaseema through Bollapalli
accepted.x: The Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar link proposes transfer of Godavari floodwater to Rayalaseema through Bollapalli.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between links by their route and purpose.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: The Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar proposal is stated to benefit approximately:
accepted.x: The proposal is associated with benefits for about 80 lakh people and 7.5 lakh acres. Telangana has objected to it.
accepted.tq: Pair the beneficiary population with the irrigated-area figure.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Vamsadhara–Nagavali link is correct?
o: It was about 73% complete and targeted June 2027
It is a five-stage lift scheme carrying 7,000 cusecs
It was about 19.32% complete and targeted June 2025
It was completed in 2014 with a target of 80 TMC
accepted.x: The Vamsadhara–Nagavali link was reported to be 73% complete, with a target of June 2027.
accepted.tq: Use status and target-date discrimination for an ongoing project.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: The Nagavali–Suvarnamukhi link, involving four rivers, is primarily intended to provide:
accepted.x: The Nagavali–Suvarnamukhi link was about 19.32% complete and is intended to provide drinking water to Vizianagaram.
accepted.tq: Identify the link from its beneficiary area and objective.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: Which of the following is the priority link identified by the National Water Development Agency?
accepted.x: The NWDA priority link runs from Godavari at Inchampalli through Krishna at Nagarjunasagar and Pennar at Somasila to the Cauvery.
accepted.tq: Follow the complete river-link sequence from north to south.
accepted.sec: River linking in AP - rivers linked

accepted.s: Since its inception, APMIP has covered approximately:

accepted.tq: Match the two related coverage figures without reversing them.

accepted.s: What is the approximate distribution of APMIP coverage between drip and sprinkler irrigation?
accepted.x: APMIP coverage consists of approximately 75% drip irrigation and 25% sprinkler irrigation.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of the percentage comparison.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding micro-irrigation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. About 1.90 lakh hectares were covered between June 2024 and December 2025.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked first nationally in micro-irrigation in 2024–25.
3. The subsidy is 100% for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: 1.90 lakh hectares were covered during the stated period, Andhra Pradesh ranked first nationally in 2024–25, and SC/ST beneficiaries receive 100% subsidy.
accepted.tq: Verify a cluster of current coverage, ranking and subsidy facts.
accepted.sec: Water use efficiency - APMIP, drip and sprinkler

accepted.s: The target for micro-irrigation as a share of gross sown area is:
accepted.x: The target is micro-irrigation over 35% of gross sown area by 2030 and 50% by 2047.
accepted.tq: Recall paired target years and percentages together.
accepted.sec: Water use efficiency - APMIP, drip and sprinkler

accepted.s: Under Per Drop More Crop, the assistance pattern for drip and sprinkler systems is:
o: 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for others
50% for small and marginal farmers and 50% for others
75% for small and marginal farmers and 25% for others
60% for small and marginal farmers and 40% for others
accepted.x: Per Drop More Crop provides 55% assistance to small and marginal farmers and 45% to other farmers.
accepted.tq: Compare beneficiary categories by their respective assistance percentages.
accepted.sec: Water use efficiency - APMIP, drip and sprinkler

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional status of Per Drop More Crop?
o: It began in 2015–16, came under RKVY from 2022–23, and covered 102 lakh hectares nationally since inception.
It was launched in 2003 and has always been under the Tungabhadra Board.
It is implemented only in Andhra Pradesh through APMIP.
It began in 2022–23 and covered 10.2 lakh hectares nationally since 2015–16.
accepted.x: Per Drop More Crop began in 2015–16, has been under RKVY since 2022–23, and covered 102 lakh hectares nationally since 2015–16.
accepted.tq: Combine programme chronology, administrative placement and national coverage.
accepted.sec: Water use efficiency - APMIP, drip and sprinkler

accepted.s: The Micro Irrigation Fund, having a corpus of ₹10,000 crore, is associated with:
o: NABARD, with Andhra Pradesh among the eight funded States
RBI, with Andhra Pradesh as the sole funded State
NWDA, with all States receiving equal funds
KRMB, with only the two Krishna-basin States receiving funds

accepted.s: Which of the following projects is correctly matched with its river and State location?
o: Damodar Valley — Damodar — Jharkhand and West Bengal
Tungabhadra — Mahanadi — Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Nagarjuna Sagar — Damodar — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
accepted.x: The Damodar Valley project is on the Damodar and is associated with Jharkhand and West Bengal. The other options reverse the river or project association.

accepted.s: Hirakud is notable as:
o: A canal-only irrigation project without a dam
The largest concrete arch dam in Asia
A tidal barrage on the Krishna
One of the longest earthen dams
accepted.x: Hirakud in Odisha is noted as one of the longest earthen dams.

accepted.s: The Krishna River Management Board and Godavari River Management Board operate under the:
o: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, with Schedule 11 principles
accepted.x: KRMB and GRMB operate under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, following the principles in Schedule 11.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-law trap to identify the governing statute.
accepted.sec: Inter-state boards - Tungabhadra Board, KRMB, GRMB

accepted.s: Which order of priority is followed for water use under the operating principles of KRMB and GRMB?
o: All uses have an identical priority
Power over irrigation, and irrigation over drinking water
Irrigation over drinking water, and power over both
Drinking water over irrigation, and irrigation over power
accepted.x: Drinking water takes precedence over irrigation, and irrigation takes precedence over power.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed-priority trap in a hierarchy question.
accepted.sec: Inter-state boards - Tungabhadra Board, KRMB, GRMB

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards:
1. The operation protocol of the Ministry of Water Resources based on KWDT adjudication is binding on both States.
2. Existing tribunal allocations remain unchanged.
3. Future excess-flow allocations are binding on both States.
4. The Boards advise on floods and droughts and have authority to enforce their orders.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the operating and enforcement principles applicable to the Boards.
accepted.tq: Treat each institutional power and allocation rule as an independent statement.
accepted.sec: Inter-state boards - Tungabhadra Board, KRMB, GRMB

accepted.s: The GWDT award of 1980 permitted diversion of how much Godavari water to the Krishna?
accepted.x: The 1980 GWDT award permitted the Polavaram diversion of 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna.
accepted.tq: Recall the tribunal-specific diversion quantity and year.
accepted.sec: Water disputes tribunals - KWDT, GWDT

accepted.s: Which concern was raised by a forum of Andhra Pradesh intellectuals regarding the Krishna water settlement with Telangana?
o: That it would eliminate all drinking-water priorities
That it would transfer the Tungabhadra Board to Karnataka
That it was being linked to Andhra Pradesh’s consent to Palamuru–Rangareddy
That it would abolish the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal
accepted.x: The concern was that the Krishna water settlement with Telangana was being linked to Andhra Pradesh’s consent to the Palamuru–Rangareddy project.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific political linkage in an inter-State water controversy.
accepted.sec: Water disputes tribunals - KWDT, GWDT
